bib.title: Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever for Question Answering

question: Can a retriever for open-domain QA be trained without query-document labels, using a reader's attention as synthetic relevance labels?
hypothesis: Reader cross-attention scores over passages are a good proxy for passage relevance.
contributions: Show that attention scores from a seq2seq reader are a good measure of document relevance (Sec 3.2)
Iteratively train the retriever from these activations, inspired by knowledge distillation, and compare loss functions (Sec 3.4)
Evaluate on three QA benchmarks with state-of-the-art results (Sec 4)

method.summary: A Fusion-in-Decoder (T5) reader is trained on retrieved passages; its first-output-token cross-attention, averaged over passage tokens, layers and heads, gives per-passage scores. A shared-encoder BERT bi-encoder retriever is trained to match these scores with a KL loss, then retrieves new passages and the loop repeats.

datasets.name: NaturalQuestions
datasets.split: original dev set used as test; 10% of train held out for validation
datasets.source: Kwiatkowski et al. 2019; Wikipedia dump of Dec. 20, 2018, 100-token non-overlapping passages
datasets.preprocessing: Questions with answers longer than five tokens discarded; preprocessing as Chen et al. 2017

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.split: original dev set used as test; 10% of train held out for validation
datasets.source: Joshi et al. 2017; same Wikipedia dump
datasets.preprocessing: Uppercase answers normalised with Python str.title

datasets.name: NarrativeQA
datasets.source: Kocisky et al. 2018, public preprocessed version; stories average 60k words, chunked into 100 words
datasets.preprocessing: Uppercase questions and answers lowercased; full-story setting, no summary

models.name: Reader: Fusion-in-Decoder base
models.architecture: T5 encoder-decoder, passages encoded separately, fused in decoder
models.context: each encoder input at most 250 tokens

models.name: Reader: Fusion-in-Decoder large
models.context: each encoder input at most 250 tokens

models.name: Retriever
models.architecture: BERT bi-encoder, shared encoder for question and passage, CLS representation, score E(q)^T E(p)/sqrt(d)

training.objective: Retriever: KL divergence between softmax of reader attention scores G and softmax of retriever scores S over the retrieved passages (MSE and max-margin compared). Reader: answer generation (standard FiD).
training.lr: 1e-4 base reader (constant); 5e-5 retriever (constant); 5e-5 peak large reader
training.lr_schedule: constant for base reader and retriever; linear warmup then linear decrease for large reader
training.steps: base reader 10k gradient steps; large reader 600 warmup + 14.4k decrease; retriever until performance saturates

other.iterations: reader reinitialised from T5 base each iteration (except Table 8); retriever training continues, never reinitialised
other.model_selection: best reader chosen on validation performance
other.monitoring: ranking similarity between reader and retriever (inversions, top-k overlap)

inference.decoding: greedy for TriviaQA and NaturalQuestions; beam search with 3 beams for NarrativeQA
inference.samples: inferred: single run per setting, no seeds or repeats reported
inference.retrieval: 100 passages via FAISS; initial passages BM25 (Lucene defaults, SpaCy tokenisation), non-finetuned BERT, or DPR

metrics.name: R@k
metrics.definition: percentage of questions where at least one of top-k retrieved passages contains the gold answer

eval.protocol: Single runs; no significance test or seeds reported. Ablations use one iteration on NQ from BM25, validation set.

limits: Authors note R@k is a doubtful retriever metric since the answer can appear in an unrelated passage.
Initial passage quality matters: BERT start performs far worse.
Attention-as-relevance is an assumption tested mainly by the top-10 selection experiment.
No seeds, variance, hardware or compute reported.
Model sizes are T5 base and large only; the Table 3 iteration is unspecified.
